title: On-demand console slices and scheduled delivery triage playbook
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Create an operational playbook and intake flow for two frequently requested enterprise capabilities: 1) on-demand 'console slices' (ad-hoc filtered usage reports delivered instantly) and 2) scheduled deliveries (recurring exports/dashboards to S3/BI connectors). The goal is to standardize triage, prioritize by enterprise SLAs, and provide clear handoffs to engineering and design. This ticket defines the scoring matrix, intake form fields, minimal product scope for MVP, rollout cadence, and acceptance criteria.
background: Over the past 18 months we've seen a rising number of customer asks for ad-hoc analytics slices and scheduled exports tied to billing reconciliation, audits, and internal cost dashboards. Current handling is ad-hoc via support and solutions engineering, causing long lead times and inconsistent outcomes. This causes high-touch support costs and unpredictable enterprise satisfaction metrics. We need a repeatable triage + delivery playbook that scales with the PLG motion while preserving enterprise guarantees.
problem_statement: Customers require predictable timelines and clear SLAs for enterprise reporting requests. We lack a consistent intake form that captures required security, delivery, and data-retention constraints, and we lack a prioritization rubric that aligns engineering capacity with business impact. Without this playbook, we continue to over-index on reactive, high-effort builds with limited reuse.
proposed_solution: Deliver a two-part playbook: 1) Intake form template embedded in Console for structured requests (required fields, red flags, routing rules). 2) Triage + prioritization matrix that maps request archetypes to delivery lanes: Self-serve (templates + docs), Configurable scheduled exports (supported by Console), and Custom engineering deliveries (work orders with SLAs). Provide runbooks for Solutions Eng to accelerate common scenarios and a 'fast-fail' checklist to push low-value asks back to self-serve.
intake_form_fields: Required: workspace_id, tenant SSO status, target recipients (S3/BigQuery/CSV email), delivery cadence, retention window, sample query or report definition, security constraints (PII, encryption required), estimated row volume, urgency (business justification), desired SLA (30d/7d/48h), contact (requestor + approver). Optional: pivot definitions, cost center tags, visualization preferences.
triage_scoring_matrix: Score requests across five dimensions (each 0-5): 1) Customer revenue impact, 2) Compliance/regulatory risk, 3) Reusability (can this be templated?), 4) Implementation effort (engineering points), 5) Operational risk (data sensitivity, access controls). Add +3 for existing Dedicated or Private workspaces. Map total score to lanes: 0-7 Self-serve docs, 8-13 Configurable Console feature/automation, 14+ Engineering work order with SLA and dedicated resource.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Intake form prototype is added to Console request flow and validated with 3 enterprise customers. 2) Triage rubric documented and validated via 5 recent historical requests (apply retrospectively). 3) Two runbook templates created for common slices (billing reconciliation, per-team cost breakdown). 4) Routing rules implemented in triage board that auto-assigns 'Configurable' to PM and 'Engineering' to ENG lead. 5) Pilot delivery with one enterprise customer: scheduled S3 export weekly, automated retry, and dashboard snapshot link.
design_considerations: Keep Console UX low-friction: progressive disclosure for advanced fields, inline help for security flags, and one-click template selection. Design to show estimated cost impact for large row exports. Ensure RBAC compatibility and KMS selection UI for Private workspaces. Coordinate with Design (DES-3309) for microcopy and help flows.
engineering_considerations: Minimal MVP for Configurable lane should reuse existing export infra and add parameterized templates + schedule engine. Need quota and throttling policy to prevent runaway exports. For Engineering lane, define API contract for ad-hoc slices, and ensure exports can be intercepted by audit/logging. Dependencies: ENG-48212 (scheduler scaling), logging-tracework to capture export runs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): build intake form prototype in Console + triage rubric doc. Phase 2 (3 sprints): implement auto-routing and Configurable scheduled export template (S3/CSV). Phase 3 (4 sprints): pilot with 3 enterprise customers, iterate on UX and runbooks, then broad rollout behind feature flag. Communication: release notes, solutions engineering playbook, and a webinar for top 20 customers.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: large exports causing cluster contention. Mitigation: quota-based throttles and queueing with backpressure. Risk: exposing PII; Mitigation: require data classification field and enforce KMS encryption for Private workspaces. Risk: high manual effort for custom deliveries; Mitigation: establish clear SLA pricing and require PO/contract for engineering lane.
metrics_and_success: KPIs: average time-to-deliver (days) per lane, % of requests resolved via self-serve, number of templated exports created, NPS change for enterprise support tickets related to reporting. Target: reduce average delivery time for Configurable lane to <=7 days and increase self-serve resolution to 60% for new reporting requests within 6 months.
open_questions: 1) Should we support direct BI connector deliveries (Looker/BigQuery) in MVP or postpone to Phase 3? 2) What pricing/chargeback model applies for 'Engineering' lane ad-hoc deliveries? 3) Do we need dedicated ingestion keys for large-volume exports?
